title: [FancyZones] Zone colors are black after restarting GPU driver
author: lasersPew
summary: Restarting the graphics driver with Win+Ctrl+Shift+B can make FancyZones use black default zone colors until appearance settings or PowerToys are reset.
next_action: Reproduce the graphics-device reset and trace theme/default brush recreation.

confidence.rationale: The reproduction and control path are explicit; only the modern graphics resource branch is unknown.

judgment.rationale: The issue has exact steps, expected/actual screenshots, and a workaround showing custom colors still render.
evidence: The failure follows the standard graphics-driver reset shortcut.
Switching to custom colors restores normal rendering; returning to defaults reproduces the black state.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the graphics-device reset and trace theme/default brush recreation.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report establishes a rendering-state loss but not whether the current overlay recreates graphics resources or theme brushes after device reset.

issue_context.summary: Restarting the graphics driver with Win+Ctrl+Shift+B can make FancyZones use black default zone colors until appearance settings or PowerToys are reset.
known_information: The issue was reported on PowerToys 0.63.0.
Custom zone colors and default Windows colors follow different paths.
inferences: A device-loss or theme-resource refresh path may leave the default brush uninitialized while explicit custom colors are rebuilt.
issue_context.analysis: The reporter has already provided the discriminating control case; maintainer-side graphics reset testing is next.
initial_investigation: Read the steps, screenshots, workaround, and maintainer question.
Confirmed current FancyZones keeps separate appearance/settings and runtime overlay code.

actions.label: Reproduce zone colors after GPU reset
actions.note: Maintainer-side verification only; this artifact performs no upstream write.

reproduce.title: Reset the graphics driver while using default FancyZones colors
prerequisites: FancyZones enabled with Windows-default zone appearance
setup: Set Overrides Windows Snap as reported.
Use default rather than custom zone colors.
steps: Press Win+Ctrl+Shift+B and wait for the display driver to recover.
Shift-drag a window to show zones.
Switch to custom colors and retest.
Switch back to defaults and record whether black returns.
reproduce.expected_result: Default and custom zone colors should both survive graphics-device reset without becoming black.
